extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large-scale multilingual dataset for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, consisting of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Audiobooks were downloaded from LibriVox using the LibriLight open source library. Text sources were downloaded from gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, and other domains using automated parsers and manual approaches.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For audiobooks with invalid links for text sources, manual online searches were conducted to find alternate sources where the book is available.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox and corresponding text sources from Project Gutenberg and other online domains.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Numbers in the matched text from the book were replaced with the corresponding aligned words from the pseudo label. Heuristics were also used to replace rare words containing hyphens and apostrophes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments by splitting at the midpoint of the longest silence chunk. Source text was split into multiple overlapping documents of 1250 words each, striding by 1000 words.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text was normalized using NFKC normalization, removing unwanted characters (punctuations, emojis, escape symbols), removing end-of-line hyphens, and filtering characters outside the valid unicode range based on the language's orthography.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo labels were generated for audio segments using beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model. Target labels were retrieved by matching pseudo labels to source text using TF-IDF similarity and Smith-Waterman alignment. For development and test sets, human transcribers listened to the audio and corrected clear and obvious errors in the transcripts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human transcribers were asked to only correct 'clear and obvious' errors to avoid adding potential bias. Word Error Rate (WER) between generated transcripts and human-rated transcripts was measured to ensure high quality.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere framework, Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss, Smith-Waterman alignment, SVM gender classifier
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender (speakers were labeled with a gender classifier to balance development and test sets)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems, multilingual ASR, and Text-to-Speech (TTS) research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: To avoid high speaker imbalance in development and test sets, speakers with high duration were truncated by sampling their recordings up to an upper-bound. Human transcribers were instructed to only correct clear and obvious errors to avoid adding potential bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The number replacement solution is not perfect as the pseudo label may not always have the correct transcription. For Polish, a high out-of-vocabulary (OOV) rate of 13% negatively impacts the WER during language model decoding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Development (Validation), and Testing of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-To-Speech (TTS) models, as well as Language Modeling.
